prompt_text: What is the best tanning salon in Tyler TX?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a UV-bed salon or a spray (sunless) tan? I can recommend options and help you pick one — but I don't have live access to local listings right now. If you tell me whether you want UV or spray, your preferred part of Tyler (zip code or neighborhood), and if price or speed matters, I’ll give a tailored short list and tips. 

Meanwhile, here’s how to pick the best tanning salon and what to ask/inspect when you call or visit:

What “best” usually means
- Cleanliness and well-maintained equipment
- Trained, friendly staff who explain session timing for your skin type
- Multiple tanning options (high-pressure beds, low-pressure beds, spray booths)
- Transparent pricing, packages, and membership terms
- Good recent customer reviews and visible safety practices

Checklist to evaluate a salon
- Read recent Google/Yelp/Facebook reviews for consistency (not just the average score).
- Check that beds are cleaned between clients and eye protection is provided.
- Ask the brand/age of tanning beds and whether they’re high-pressure or high-intensity (older beds can be less safe/effective).
- For spray tans: ask about solution brands, whether technicians are certified, and whether a patch test is available.
- Ask about staff training, session length recommendations by skin type, and how they minimize overexposure.
- Look for clear cancellation policies and no hidden fees for packages.

Questions to ask when you call
- “What types of tanning options do you offer (beds, stand-up booth, spray)?”
- “How long are the typical sessions for my skin type (I = fair, II, III etc.)?”
- “How often do you recommend coming in, and what safety precautions do you follow?”
- “Do you offer packages/memberships and are there any long-term commitments?”
- “Can I see customer photos or reviews of spray tans?”

Safety reminders
- Tanning beds increase the risk of skin cancer and premature aging; consider spray tans as a safer alternative.
- Never exceed the time recommended for your skin type.
- Don’t use tanning beds if you’ve been prescribed photosensitizing medication without a doctor’s okay.
- Always use eye protection in UV beds and remove makeup for spray tans.

If you want, tell me:
- UV or spray?
- Your part of Tyler or zip code
- Any budget or scheduling constraints

I’ll then give targeted salon suggestions and what to look for in each.
